# Data Quality Scorecard: Trade Signal core dataset + raw CRM export

**Assessed by:** Ian Castorillo, using the vendored `data-quality-audit` Claude Code skill (see `.claude/skills/README.md`)
**Date:** 2026-09-06
**Table / dataset:** `data/customers.csv`, `data/funnel_events.csv`, `data/email_engagement.csv`, `data/reviews.csv` (canonical synthetic dataset), plus `data/raw_crm_export.csv` → `data/customers_reconciled.csv` (the deliberately messy CRM-export reconciliation exercise)
**Pipeline / source:** Static, point-in-time synthetic dataset generated by `data/generate_dataset.py` (seed=42); not a live pipeline
**Assessment scope:** Full tables (3,200 customers, 8,868 funnel events, 7,949 email engagements, 474 reviews, 669 raw CRM export rows)

---

## Quality Dimension Scores

Timeliness is scored **N/A**, not a low number — this is a static, generated-once dataset, not a live pipeline with an SLA, so "freshness" doesn't apply in its usual sense (see Checks Performed below for what was actually checked). The overall score is a weighted average of the other five dimensions, with their weights renormalized to sum to 100%.

| Dimension | Weight | Score (0–10) | Weighted | Key Issues |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Completeness | 20% → 23.5% | 9 | 2.12 | `company_name` is 76% null overall — but 100% populated for trade/commercial and 100% null for homeowner/designer; the null rate exactly mirrors segment mix, not a data gap |
| Accuracy | 20% → 23.5% | 10 | 2.35 | All three business-rule checks (amount ≥ 0, email_opt_in ∈ {0,1}, review score 1–10) pass with zero violations |
| Consistency | 20% → 23.5% | 10 | 2.35 | All three referential-integrity checks (funnel_events, email_engagement, reviews → customers) pass with 0 orphan rows out of 17,291 combined child rows |
| Uniqueness | 15% → 17.6% | 8 | 1.41 | Canonical dataset is clean (customer_id 100% unique, 0 full-row duplicates); the intentionally-messy raw CRM export needs base-ID normalization to find its real duplicates — see Medium finding below |
| Validity | 10% → 11.8% | 10 | 1.18 | Same three rule checks as Accuracy (this project's rules are both range and domain checks) — 0 violations |
| **Overall** | **100%** | | **9.41 / 10** | |
| Timeliness | (excluded) | N/A | — | Static synthetic dataset — see Checks Performed |

**Overall verdict:** PASS (≥ 7.0)

---

## Critical Findings (must fix before production use)

None found.

## High Severity (fix within 5 business days)

None found.

## Medium / Low (document and monitor)

| # | Dimension | Finding | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Uniqueness | `duplicate_finder.py --key customer_id` reports **0 duplicates** on `raw_crm_export.csv` — correct on the literal column, but misleading: the file's 68 real duplicate customers are encoded as separate `customer_id` values carrying a `-dup` or `-nochan` suffix (e.g. `CUST-00042` and `CUST-00042-dup`), not exact-matching keys. Re-deriving the base ID (stripping those suffixes, the same normalization `data/reconcile_crm_export.py` already does) finds exactly **600 unique base IDs from 669 raw rows, 68 appearing more than once** — independently reproducing `docs/measurement-foundation.md`'s published "669→600, 68 merged" figure via a completely different method. A generic duplicate-key check can't know a suffix encodes intentional duplication without being told; this project's own reconciliation script already handles it correctly. | Documented, no action needed — flagging so the generic tool's blind spot doesn't get mistaken for "this data has no duplicates" |
| 2 | Uniqueness / Consistency | 7 of the 92 live HubSpot↔Salesforce matches (7.6% of matches, 1.7% of 403 candidate pairs) are fuzzy name+company matches between genuinely different people (e.g. HubSpot "Patricia Okafor" ↔ Salesforce "Priya Okafor"; confidence 85–93%). Already fully documented in `analysis/crm-reconciliation/output/reconciliation_findings.md` | Pulled directly from `analysis/crm-reconciliation/output/reconciliation_report.json`, not re-detected. Severity LOW — known mechanism, known rate, not an open question |
| 3 | Accuracy (informational, not a defect) | `outlier_detector.py --method both` flags 311 of 1,654 non-null `amount` values (18.8%) as IQR outliers in `funnel_events.csv`. All 311 belong to the trade (228) or commercial (83) segments — 0 from homeowner or designer — even though those two segments make up only 19.4% of all purchases. This is the expected shape of a population that mixes very different order sizes by segment, not a data-entry problem | Documented, no action needed |
| 4 | Completeness | `region` is 3.38% null in `data/customers.csv` (108 of 3,200 rows) — below the 5% WARN threshold, fully recovered (0% null) in `data/customers_reconciled.csv` via the coalescing logic in `reconcile_crm_export.py` | Documented, no action needed |

## Checks Performed

| Check | Script | Result | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| Null audit | `null_counter.py` (imported directly — see note below) | 1 FAIL of 7 columns | `company_name` fails the generic 20% threshold at 76% null, fully explained by segment (see Completeness above) |
| Duplicate detection | `duplicate_finder.py` | PASS (literal), see Medium #1 | 0 full-row and 0 exact-key duplicates on `raw_crm_export.csv`'s `customer_id` — real duplication exists under suffixed IDs, see above |
| Referential integrity | `referential_integrity.py` | PASS × 3 | 0 orphan rows across funnel_events→customers (8,868 rows), email_engagement→customers (7,949 rows), reviews→customers (474 rows) |
| Value range validation | `value_range_validator.py` | PASS × 3 | `amount ≥ 0` (funnel_events), `email_opt_in ∈ {0,1}` (customers), `score ∈ [1,10]` (reviews) — 0 violations |
| Freshness | `freshness_check.py` | PASS, N/A in spirit | Latest record is 2025-08-31; run against a deliberately generous 999,999-hour SLA since this is a static, point-in-time synthetic dataset, not a live pipeline — the check runs cleanly but "freshness" isn't a meaningful concept here. Included for completeness rather than skipped silently |

**Note on `null_counter.py`:** this vendored script (and its `programmatic-eda` counterpart `null_profiler.py`) crash under Python 3.14 when invoked via its CLI, including with real arguments — not just `--help` — because argparse's stricter help-string validation trips on a bare `%` character in one of its `help=` strings (`"JSON dict of column -> max acceptable null %"`). This is an upstream bug in the vendored skill, not something specific to this project's data. Rather than patch the vendored file (see `.claude/skills/README.md`'s policy on not editing vendored skills in place), both scripts' core functions (`count_nulls`, `profile_nulls`) were imported directly and called in Python, bypassing the broken CLI entirely — see `analysis/data-quality-audit/output/raw_script_output/null_checks_direct_import.txt` and `null_counter_clean.txt` for the captured runs.

Full captured stdout from every script run is in `analysis/data-quality-audit/output/raw_script_output/`.
